newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken says income hurt by interest rate margins.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken says income hurt by interest rate margins.

text.p: Sweden's state-controlled bank, Nordbanken, Thursday posted a 21 percent fall in operating profit for the first half of 1997, hit by continuing pressure on interest rate margins.
Nordbanken reported an operating profit of 3.02 billion crowns ($378.4 million), largely in line with market expectations of 3.08 billion crowns ($385.9 million).
Loan losses fell to 194 million crowns ($24.3 million) from 260 million crowns ($32.6 million) in the corresponding year-earlier period. Analysts had expected them to be largely unchanged.
The decline in profits compared with a strong first half of 1996, which was partly lifted by sharply falling interest rates that boosted the bank's bond portfolio, the bank said in a statement.
Net interest income fell by 7 percent to 4.92 billion crowns ($616.4 million), hurt by lower interest rate margins and a higher fee for the government's bank guarantee.
"Higher volumes could not fully compensate for lower margins," the bank said.
